If you don't mind, I'd like to ask you something IF for clarification,
 that's been a source of mild confusion to me for some time.

In the diagram (very simplified), there are 2 FO scenarios. Scenario 1
is very clear, and predictable FO. Scenario 2 however - price engulfs
the seemingly more important FL, and bounces from a more minor one. Is
this a valid FO, and we should therefore treat the resultant move north
with the same significance as if it had originated from the important
FL? Or is this genuine engulf south?

Let's say for arguments sake in scenario 2, the "important" high is the
top of the last significant downward FTR of a bear move before reversal
north - so not just a random high, but an important level.

Thanks for any help, even if it's just a cryptic comment ;-)

author: Raj
text:
Hi Smimon:

Here is my take on your diagram. When price engulfs your "more important
 FL" the logical expectation then would be a slide to the next demand
zone which is the "Less important FL" in your chart. So, for me, price
has reached its logical destination after the engulf or rather fakeout.
 I view it more as stacked demand and it is always better to wait for
the price to reach the lower of the two stacked levels. The higher level
 is a prime case for faking-out. Whether you want to call the "Less
important FL" as a FL or DP is again up to you. Just nomenclature I
guess. Point is, there is pent-up demand in that area.

Caveat: Am a newbie at RTM and hence could have lots of loose ends in my understanding.

Regards

Raj

Thank you for the reply, but at the risk of cluttering up IF's journal
further, perhaps we should just wait for his comment on the matter.

Raj - and this is something else IF may need to clarify - "decision" to
engulf a level is not a high probability level to trade on return in the
 same way that a FL is. Yes, they do bounce price some of the time, but
they do not have the significance of a FL. If you note, there is no
article on the Markepedia about DP being a valid high probability
tradeable level.

Everyone talks about them here on RTM all the time - usually to
backwards justify when something happened which they weren't expecting
;-) "Oh, it was FO into DP!"

I was just after a clear "yes this is valid FO/no it is not/it is not
possible to tell until more PA plays out", to remove a source of
ambiguity from my trading and adjust my trade execution accordingly.

Cheers

author: Ptpatrader
text:
That area you point to was the FO level on the HTF, right before price
 fell away. On the HTF price hasnt been back here, so one thing you do
is look for the likely places where there was a clear turning point. If
 you look at IF's Nov chart you can clearly see the primary FO level
before price fell away. You want to remember that location when the HTF
 works its way out and the instrument heads back up.

Also keep in mind that IF used words like "on approach..." Thats gold.
 As price came up to that level there are some very good indicators that
 a trade was on the table. If your goal is to learn to make money, than
 I wouldnt be concerned with IF's to-the-pip entry; he's a grand master.
 For the journeymen, IMO the real focus was understanding the levels to
 be interested in when GU finally gets up to this major level, and then
be ready for any factors that are simple to monitor and identify. The
engulf was clear. the huge rally into the level was clear. A huge
rally into a major supply level. If you didnt manage to get in on
spike, the hesitation that IF mentions was absolutely worth jumping in
on in my view due to the engulf lower to the left. Added to this is
that the target was textbook....in fact I see a nice long up to supply
before taking the short back down, but thats just me.

Also pay attention to how IF got out...monitoring the moves/ reading
price. IF highlights the engulf, and the obvious question is why did it
 then make a lower low....but alas it still rises back to supply. Savvy
 trades will see there is at least 1:3 RR trade back up from this move
down, and worthy of the punt. That 1:3 actually turns into a 1:10 or so
 if the PA was being read well, back up to supply.
